summary: All three copy corrections work and are proven on a live Perps Pro device run (22/22 recipe nodes, 3/3 claims PROVEN, 107/107 unit tests, tsc clean). One fix-before-merge item: the new formatOrderTypeLabel renders hardcoded English and raw provider strings, dropping the i18n and provider normalization the removed helper had.

comments.body:
This helper drops both the translation and the provider normalization that the removed `getOrderTypeLabel` provided, so the pill is now un-translated and provider-dependent.

**i18n regression.** The old code returned `strings('perps.order.market')` for the market fallback and `strings('...open_limit'/'close_limit')` for limit orders. This returns the English literals `'Limit'` / `'Market'`. `perps.order.market` and `perps.order.limit` already exist and are translated in 13 locales (`de, el, es, fr, hi, id, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, vi, zh` — e.g. fr `Marché` / `Limite`), so those users previously saw translated copy on this pill and will now see English.

**Provider leak.** `order.detailedOrderType` is provider-supplied and is rendered verbatim. HyperLiquid emits exactly the canonical `DETAILED_ORDER_TYPES` values (`Stop Market`, `Take Profit Limit`, …), but the MYX adapter (`@metamask/perps-controller/utils/myxAdapter.mjs:308-317`) emits `'Take Profit'`, `'Stop Loss'`, `'Liquidation'` — none of which are in that set. Once MYX orders reach this tab, the same UI will read `Stop loss` beside HyperLiquid's `Stop market`. The removed helper normalized both to `Stop`. The perps anti-pattern guide is explicit that provider differences must be normalized in the aggregation layer, not leaked to the view.

**Suggested fix.** Minimum: use `strings('perps.order.limit')` / `strings('perps.order.market')` for the fallback branch. Better: map `detailedOrderType` through `DETAILED_ORDER_TYPES` to i18n keys — it is a closed six-value set, so the map stays small and the pill becomes both translated and provider-independent.

Worth adding a test that asserts the label is resolved through `strings(...)`, since the current suites pass on English literals and so cannot catch this class of regression.

Removing `getOrderTypeLabel` and switching the side filter to `all_sides` orphaned five keys in this file — they now have zero references anywhere in `app/` (verified by ripgrep):

- `perps.pro_positions_panel.side_filter.all_types` (line 1551)
- `perps.pro_positions_panel.order_card.take_profit` (line 1581)
- `perps.pro_positions_panel.order_card.stop` (line 1582)
- `perps.pro_positions_panel.order_card.open_limit` (line 1583)
- `perps.pro_positions_panel.order_card.close_limit` (line 1584)

These are orphans this change created, so removing them here keeps the locale bundle and the translation pipeline from carrying dead strings. (If any are intentionally kept for the `formatOrderTypeLabel` i18n fix suggested on `orderUtils.ts`, please keep them and disregard.)

This `Tag` has no `testID`, which makes the copy the PR is fixing unassertable by automated validation. I hit this directly while validating: `ui.wait_for` against the order-row testID returns only the row's own shallow text (`"BTC"`), so there is no way to assert the pill string — claim 2 had to fall back to screenshot plus unit-test proof instead of a typed UI assertion.

Since this PR already modifies this element, please add a `testID` sourced from `Perps.testIds.ts` (e.g. `PerpsProMarketViewSelectorsIDs.ORDER_TYPE_TAG`) so recipes and E2E can read the value. The perps testID convention asks for the testID to sit on the element that actually holds the value, i.e. the `Tag` rather than a wrapper.

This type-resolution expression is character-for-character identical to the one in `formatOrderLabel` just above (lines 566-567). Worth extracting a small internal helper (e.g. `resolveOrderTypeString(order)`) that both call, so the two labels cannot drift apart — particularly relevant if the i18n/normalization fix above is applied to only one of them.
